SELENOK deficiency inhibits melanomas by reducing the Ca2+ flux needed for tumor growth and progression.

the role of SELENOK in melanoma, which is the most deadly form of skin cancer.
the role of the calcium channel protein IP3R in the development of melanoma.
the role of SELENOK in Ca2+ flux, which is required for the development and progression of melanoma, and suggests a novel therapeutic target for treating this disease.

the results presented in this thesis provide the first evidence that SELENOK deficiency inhibits Ca2+-flux and melanoma growth and metastasis in vivo and in vitro, thus revealing a novel therapeutic approach to treating melanoma.
SELENOK is a new therapeutic target for melanoma and possibly for other cancers.

we show that melanoma cells require SELENOK for IP3R function which is required for Ca2+ flux, which is required for tumor growth, stemness and metastasis.

The main takeaway from our work is that

melanoma cells require SELENOK expression to efficiently activate IP3R and maintain stemness, which is required for tumor growth, and that SELENOK-deficient cells exhibit a strong reduction in Ca2+ flux, calcineurin activity, stemness, and metastasis.
SELENOK is required for Ca2+ flux in melanoma and that SELENOK inhibition can be used as a therapeutic approach to inhibit melanoma and other types of cancer.
